[Mike] (turnIndex=142, startMs=2353800, endMs=2383380) Look, I Think it's a little bit different.The corporate decisions And knowledge That underlie The Teamwork graph Are about us trying to help a company That Has made decisions, projects, documents, data often.For example, How many times Are PowerPoint slides The place Where People put actual facts And figures?A lot.But, Like, data is stored in databases.
[Mike] (turnIndex=143, startMs=2383380, endMs=2418455) I'm Like, Yeah, There's a lot of data stored in PowerPoints.And it didn't Actually ever Make it to a database.How do we take All of That organizational knowledge, history, decision making, wrap it into a social graph of The People in The organization, And add code, The technological services created by a company And mix All That together so we Can give You Great answers And learnings And decisions.And There's lot of inference we Can apply on Top on behalf of The company, as Well as Being a continual self learning.Right?
[Mike] (turnIndex=144, startMs=2418455, endMs=2440660) The Teamwork Graph's job is to infer ahead of Your agent Before Your agent is asked a question to infer The best possible answer to That.Think about it Like Google's index of The web.It doesn't go And crawl All of Those websites to answer Your question.It Does That in advance.It Has a lot of Really smart indexing And inference technology to create an index so That it Can answer questions Very cheaply And at scale.
[Mike] (turnIndex=145, startMs=2440820, endMs=2457740) That's Our job, But tailored For Every single company That Has a wholly different set of information.That's Very unique to each individual company.I Don't Think They're going to sell That information.I'm Not Sure it's particularly useful.I Know we saw Makar or Google.
[Mike] (turnIndex=146, startMs=2457740, endMs=2468620) I Forget Who Actually end up winning buying The SAB.It Was in Southwest.It Was Spirit.Spirit Airlines data.You Know, $30,000,000 For a million emails And a bunch of Other sort of corporate data.
[Mike] (turnIndex=147, startMs=2469180, endMs=2497140) I Don't Know if That Will become a trend, But I Think The Value of That data inside a company is Very much The same.The important Part is That it's alive.So The social graph of a company is valid Today And only Today.Tomorrow, There Will be different People in a company than There were Today.Some People left, Some People joined, And The social graph is going to continue to shift And change in terms of Who works With Who on Which projects on Which areas.
[Mike] (turnIndex=148, startMs=2497540, endMs=2523000) Our job Actually is to be Very fresh With That graph.It's Not it's to take history And to infer learnings from it.But That Has to be fresh And constantly Built on Top of.I Say This All The time When it comes to Our memory And Our dreaming And How we understand The history of an organization.Knowing That I wrote Java code in 2003, And What code I wrote is Totally useless to Atlassian in 2026.
[Mike] (turnIndex=149, startMs=2523640, endMs=2545540) Knowing The fact That I used to be a programmer, a bad One Twenty plus Years ago is kind of useful Because You May explain a concept to me in a Way That a technology savvy person Would understand.That's about as useful as it is.Right?Today, I'm a full time manager of People And my full time storyteller.I am a Part time dabbler in design And experience And products.
[Mike] (turnIndex=150, startMs=2545540, endMs=2549780) Right?That...That's That's my job.And I love my job.But The history of it is Very different.
